description.value: The study compared subcortical volumes and subcortical surface morphology between alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls using 3T structural MRI, FSL volumetric analysis, and vertex analysis.

spans.text: We analyzed the volumes of 14 subcortical structures (bilateral thalamus, caudate, putamen, globus pallidus, hippocampus, amygdala, nucleus accumbens) in 21 alcohol-dependent subjects and 21 healthy controls using images acquired with 3T MRI.

description.value: Observational cross-sectional comparison of alcohol-dependent patients and healthy controls.

value: MANCOVA showed significant volumetric reductions in alcohol-dependent patients compared with healthy controls in the bilateral thalamus, bilateral putamen, right globus pallidus, bilateral hippocampus, and bilateral nucleus accumbens. Alcohol-dependent patients also had significant reductions in gray and white matter.

value: Vertex analysis showed significant subcortical volumetric reductions in alcohol-dependent patients in the bilateral thalamus, bilateral putamen, right globus pallidus, right hippocampus, left caudate, and bilateral nucleus accumbens. The reductions matched the volumetric analysis except for the left hippocampus and left caudate. The hippocampal reductions overlapped the presubiculum, hippocampal tail, hippocampal molecular layer, hippocampal fissure, fimbria, and CA3; thalamic reductions overlapped almost every defined thalamic substructure.

spans.text: Vertex analysis showed significant subcortical volumetric reductions of alcohol-dependent patients in the bilateral thalamus, bilateral putamen, right globus pallidus, right hippocampus, left caudate, and bilateral nucleus accumbens.
Figure 2A  shows each individual subcortical structure (light blue) overlaid on top of coronal, sagittal and axial MNI152 space, with yellow areas representing significant reductions.
